questions.q: Why does a DaemonSet spec have no `replicas` field?
options: It is a typo in the Kubernetes API that was never fixed
A DaemonSet runs exactly one Pod per matching node automatically, so there's no total count to specify
DaemonSets are deprecated and no longer support replicas
replicas is only required for Jobs, not DaemonSets
questions.explain: A DaemonSet's guarantee is 'one Pod on every node,' not a specific total — so there's nothing to count. It automatically schedules a Pod onto any new node that joins the cluster.

questions.q: How does a Job's behavior differ from a Deployment's when its Pods complete successfully?
options: A Job immediately creates replacement Pods to maintain a count, just like a Deployment
A Job considers itself done and does not restart Pods that already succeeded; it tracks completions, not a standing replica count
A Job deletes itself the moment it is created
There is no functional difference
questions.explain: A Job tracks completions. Once its Pods exit successfully, it's finished — unlike a Deployment, which continuously maintains a replica count forever.

questions.q: What does `backoffLimit: 3` on a Job control?
options: The maximum number of replicas the Job can create
The maximum number of retries for a failing Pod before Kubernetes marks the whole Job as failed
The number of nodes the Job can run on
How many seconds to wait before starting the Job
questions.explain: backoffLimit caps how many times Kubernetes will retry a Job's Pod after failures before giving up and marking the Job itself as failed.

questions.q: What does a CronJob actually create when its schedule fires?
options: A new Pod directly, bypassing Jobs entirely
A new Job, which in turn creates the Pod(s) that run to completion
A new Deployment
A new DaemonSet
questions.explain: A CronJob is a scheduler wrapper around Job — on each scheduled trigger, it creates a fresh Job, which then creates and manages the Pod(s) for that run.

questions.q: Northbridge needs a log-shipping agent running on every node in its cluster, including ones added later by autoscaling. Which object fits?
options: Deployment
StatefulSet
DaemonSet
CronJob
questions.explain: DaemonSet is specifically designed to guarantee exactly one Pod per matching node, automatically extending to any new node that joins the cluster — the standard pattern for node-level agents like log collectors.
